newsitem.title: CHINA: China ship enters Taiwan port with host port flag.
newsitem.headline: China ship enters Taiwan port with host port flag.

text.p: The second ship to sail directly to Taiwan from rival China in 48 years entered the southern Kaohsiung harbour on Sunday, flying a Nationalist Republic of China flag as required.
A harbour control official confirmed the identity of the Chinese-owned Far East Glory and a Reuters reporter at the scene said the ship was flying Taiwan's flag.
A dispute over the flag had postponed the arrival of Far East Glory, which had moored outside Kaohsiung port for five hours before entering at sunset.

Although Saturday's long-awaited first crossing from China to Taiwan went smoothly, problems emerged on Sunday as the second ship to make the voyage grappled with a maritime custom which calls for ships to fly the flag of their host port.
Taiwan split from China following a civil war in 1949 and Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province.
On Saturday, the Sheng Da made an historic voyage to Taiwan after the rival sides on the Taiwan Strait eased restrictions on shipping.

The Sheng Da removed Taiwan's Republic of China flag after briefly flying it as it entered Kaohsiung port. Taiwan harbour officials later said the flag was removed because the Sheng Da entered Taiwan at night.
